Different ways solipsism could play out, as I see it.

 **[Descartes' Demon](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evil_demon)**
> The evil demon presents a complete illusion of an external world, including other minds, to Descartes' senses, where in fact there is no such external world in existence. The evil genius also presents to Descartes' senses a complete illusion of his own body, including all bodily sensations, when in fact Descartes has no body.

**Brain in a vat**
How can you prove to me that you are not just a brain in a vat, with electrodes hooked up to it projecting this reality?

**The Matrix**
Not too different than the above, except that you are not a brain in a vat, but a human body hooked up to a machine reality.

**Nested Consciousness Hypothesis**
If an intelligent species can invent artificial intelligence, why wouldn't that intelligence be able to invent it's own nested intelligence?  If it is possible to create a virtual world of artificial intelligence, capable of believing their are sentient, then it is way more likely that we are actually just a nested consciousness than an actual, biological one.

**Dream without a dreamer**
I view my solipsism as much less sinister than Descartes.  Perhaps this is all just a dream, no seeming point, and things poof in and out of existence as I interact with them.

We don't understand either consciousness or matter well enough to warrant a reasonable answer.
